feedback.problem:
Find a direction vector of the line that is given as the intersection of the following two planes:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+3y+10=0 \\ 2x-2y+z+15=0\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we notice:

- For the plane $2x+3y+10=0,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{1}=⟨2,3,0⟩.$

- For the plane $2x-2y+z+15=0,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{2}=⟨2,-2,1⟩.$

To find a direction vector for the line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={n}_{1}\times {n}_{2} \\  & =⟨2,3,0⟩\times ⟨2,-2,1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =3i-2j-10k \\  & =⟨3,-2,-10⟩\end{aligned}
$$
